risks.risk: Not actually working (e.g., HDMI/USB faults, disc drive issues, overheating, or controller drift). Photos don’t confirm functionality.
risks.proof: A short video of the console powering on, reaching the PS4 home screen, and playing a game or showing settings without errors.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: treat as needs testing/possible faults).

risks.risk: Wrong model/variant or storage size (PS4 Slim vs other PS4, and HDD capacity affects value).
risks.proof: Photo of the console label showing model number (CUH-xxxx) and storage/HDD details, or a screenshot from Settings > System > System Information.
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic PS4 Slim with unknown storage (worst case: lower-capacity/uncertain).

risks.risk: Controller bundle mismatch (seller says extra pad, but only one controller is visible).
risks.proof: Photo showing both controllers side-by-side, including their serial/model markings if possible.

risks.risk: Missing accessories/cables (power cable, HDMI cable, charging cable, original box).
risks.proof: Photo laid out showing every included item (power cable, HDMI, both controllers, any extra cables/box).
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming minimal essentials only (worst case: missing some accessories).

proof_requests: Power-on proof: short video to PS4 home screen (no errors).
System Information screenshot (storage capacity and model details).
Clear photos of both controllers (if there is an extra pad).
Photo of all included accessories laid out (power/HDMI/cables/box).
response.reason: The photo identifies a PS4-style console and a controller, but it does not prove it is working, does not confirm the exact PS4 Slim variant/storage, and the “extra pad” claim isn’t supported by the visible bundle. To price confidently, we need power-on and bundle proof.
